name: The Jefferson Washington DC
positioning: Independent hotel in a 1923 Beaux-Arts building in Washington DC, steps from the White House
best_for: Travelers who want a historic base steps from the White House
Couples considering a top-floor suite with a gas fireplace and balconies

facts.text: The Jefferson started life as a luxury apartment block in 1923.
The building was designed by architect Jules Henri de Sibour in the Beaux-Arts style.
By 1955 the apartments had been transformed into a hotel.
The Jefferson was reborn as a hotel in 2009.
The Jefferson is an independent hotel.
The hotel is steps from the White House.
The First Lady Suite has a gas fireplace, an intimate dining room and a canopied king-size bed.
The Presidential Suite has a private kitchen and a private study.
The hotel describes itself as pet-welcoming, with special amenities for dogs.
The fitness center has cardio equipment including two Pelotons and a TRX Training Center.
Quill, the bar, pairs cocktails with live piano and has private cabinet rooms and a cigar-friendly patio.

highlights.text: During the renovation, a lobby skylight that was part of the original design and hidden since World War II was recovered.
The Presidential Suite overlooks the Washington Monument and downtown DC from five Juliette balconies.
The First Lady Suite is a top-floor suite with city views and three Juliette balconies.
The Book Room surrounds guests with leather-bound books, a place to relax in privacy.
For every room booked, the hotel sponsors a children's book for the DC Public Library's Books from Birth program, with Dolly Parton's Imagination Library.

considerations.text: Pool access is through the University Club, where guests can use the pool and an expanded fitness center.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing reflecting the luxury positioning.
WhataHotel notes limited hotel amenities due to the boutique size.
